title: GPU Lossy Compression for HPC Can Be Versatile and Ultra-Fast
problem: HPC data volumes from scientific simulations grow exponentially, creating I/O and storage bottlenecks. Lossy compression reduces data size significantly, but existing GPU compression tools lack versatility (limited to specific data types) or throughput (cannot match data generation rates).
motivation: Modern simulations generate data at rates exceeding I/O and storage capacity. Compression essential for data management, but must handle diverse scientific data domains and execute at ultra-high throughput. GPU acceleration critical for viable compression throughput.
method: VGC (Versatile GPU Compression) framework supporting three compression algorithms with dimension awareness: (1) Capture data dimensional structure, (2) Optimized GPU kernels for high throughput with error control, (3) Two distinctive operational modes: memory-efficient compression and selective decompression.
key_novelty: First GPU compression framework combining versatility across domains with ultra-fast throughput via architecture-optimized kernels.
contributions: Support for three compression algorithms across diverse HPC domains
Memory-efficient compression mode using kernel fission for minimal GPU memory
Selective decompression with early stopping for region-of-interest access
limitations: Abstract-only; specific compression algorithms, throughput measurements, and compression ratios not detailed.
